findings.description: `prepare_tools` returns `crate::Result`, but the changed helper now returns `Result<_, FileWriteError>` and no `From<FileWriteError> for crate::Error` is defined. Every changed call still uses `?`, so compiling the Linux AppImage module fails with E0277 instead of producing the bundler.
findings.failureMode: On a Linux build of tauri-bundler, type-checking any `write_and_make_executable(...)?` call fails because `FileWriteError` cannot be converted to `error::Error`.
findings.title: Convert the helper error into the bundler error

findings.description: The helper now calls `set_permissions` before `fs::write`. The AppRun, linuxdeploy, GStreamer, and appimage-plugin branches call it when their target is absent, so a clean AppImage tool cache gets `ENOENT` on `set_permissions` and bundling stops before any tool or inlined plugin is created. Restore the write-then-chmod order.
findings.failureMode: Building an AppImage with an empty tool cache fails at the first missing AppRun file with a not-found permissions error.
findings.title: Write new tools before changing their permissions

findings.description: The new condition is inverted: it writes the embedded GTK script only when the cache file already exists. With a clean tools directory, `prepare_tools` leaves `linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh` absent, yet every AppImage invocation requests `--plugin gtk`; the downloaded linuxdeploy image bundles only the appimage plugin, so plugin discovery fails. Use `if !gtk.exists()` (or write it unconditionally).
findings.failureMode: Any AppImage build using a clean local/cache tools directory reaches linuxdeploy without the mandatory GTK plugin and fails with `Could not find plugin: gtk`.
findings.title: Create the inlined GTK plugin when it is missing

findings.description: `FileWriteError` is a newly introduced custom error enum, but it manually implements `Display` and `Error`. This directly violates the repository's mandatory structured-error rule requiring custom error enums to derive `thiserror::Error` with `#[error(...)]` attributes; use the existing `thiserror` dependency instead.
findings.failureMode: The changed Rust source fails the repository's mandatory error-type compliance gate/review because the new custom error is implemented manually rather than through thiserror.
findings.title: Derive the custom error with thiserror

findings.description: The newly added 101-column `set_permissions(...).map_err(...)` line is reformatted into a multiline chain by rustfmt, so the mandatory `cargo fmt --all -- --check` gate reports a diff. Run the repository formatter after correcting the helper.
findings.failureMode: The mandatory Rust formatting check fails on the changed helper line.
findings.title: Apply rustfmt to the new helper

findings.description: The new GTK source file is indented with four spaces, while the repository-wide EditorConfig and mandatory source-file rule require two-space indentation. Reindent this vendored script so EditorConfig validation accepts it.
findings.failureMode: EditorConfig/compliance validation rejects the newly added GTK script because its indented blocks do not use the mandated two-space indentation.
findings.title: Use the mandated indentation in the GTK script

findings.description: The new GStreamer source file is indented with four spaces, while the repository-wide EditorConfig and mandatory source-file rule require two-space indentation. Reindent this vendored script so EditorConfig validation accepts it.
findings.failureMode: EditorConfig/compliance validation rejects the newly added GStreamer script because its indented blocks do not use the mandated two-space indentation.

findings.description: When ToolbarMiddleware dispatches `showReaderMode` for a normal tap, this reducer now sets `displayView` to `.readerModeLongPressAction`; BrowserViewController handles that by calling `toggleReaderModeLongPressAction()` instead of `toggleReaderMode()`. A normal reader-mode tap therefore opens the long-press/add-to-reading-list flow rather than toggling reader mode. Restore `.readerMode` here.
findings.failureMode: Tap the reader-mode toolbar button on a page where reader mode is available; the app executes the long-press action instead of entering reader mode.
findings.title: Reader-mode taps now invoke the long-press action

findings.description: On a reader-mode tab, `selectedTab.url` is the internal `http://localhost/reader-mode/page?...` URL. URL-change handling normally stores `tab.url?.displayURL` (the decoded original page) in toolbar state, but the new `|| currentURL.isReaderModeURL` branch passes the raw internal URL in the cancel-edit action; `handleCancelEditAction` replaces state with it and `LocationView` renders that URL's `absoluteString`. Cancelling address editing, or opening tabs/menu while in reader mode, therefore exposes the localhost reader URL instead of restoring the article URL. Restore the prior reader-mode URL exclusion.
findings.failureMode: Enter reader mode, edit the address field, then cancel editing; the location field is restored to the internal localhost reader-mode URL rather than the original article URL.
findings.title: Keep internal reader URLs out of the address bar

findings.description: `ToolbarTelemetry.readerModeButtonTapped` currently writes its `isEnabled` argument into the event's `isPrivate` field. With the changed `default: true`, a normal-mode tap in the default nil/active reader state now records `isPrivate == true`, so the existing middleware test fails; conversely, `.available` in a private tab records false. Restore `.available: true` and `default: false` here.
findings.failureMode: Tap reader mode in a normal tab whose reader state is nil/active (including the existing default-state test); telemetry reports private browsing as true, and the existing assertion fails.
findings.title: Reader-mode events now misreport private mode

findings.description: This change drops the explicit `private` modifier from an implementation-only dependency, exposing `gleanWrapper` throughout the Client module. That violates the repository's mandatory explicit/minimal access-control rule and widens the telemetry helper's API unintentionally; keep this property `private`.
findings.failureMode: After this change, unrelated Client-module code can directly access ToolbarTelemetry's injected Glean wrapper, so the property is no longer information-hidden as required by the repository access-control contract.
findings.title: Restore private access for the telemetry dependency

findings.description: With tab swiping enabled, the right skeleton starts at the container's trailing edge and has width `container.width - 32`. This changed line places the toolbar's leading edge at that skeleton's far edge while the next line places its trailing edge at the skeleton's near edge, deriving a negative toolbar width entirely outside/reversed from the container. Keep the leading edge attached to `leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor`, which equals the container's leading edge.
findings.failureMode: On phones enrolled in the swiping-tabs experiment, the real address toolbar is laid out with reversed/out-of-container horizontal geometry.
findings.title: Anchor the toolbar between both skeleton bars

findings.description: `updateActionStack` initializes every button newly inserted into a stack with `alpha = 0`. This changed list includes `browserActionStack` twice and omits `trailingPageActionStack`, so on initial toolbar configuration the normal reload/stop/reader actions remain fully transparent (and alpha-zero views do not receive touches) in both animated and non-animated paths. Replace the final term with `trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews`.
findings.failureMode: Normal trailing address-toolbar actions render transparent and cannot be tapped after configuration.
findings.title: Restore trailing actions to the alpha update list

findings.description: The divider is constrained immediately before `trailingPageActionStack`, but this changed predicate checks the unrelated leading stack. A reachable loading or cancel-edit state has a reload/stop action in the trailing stack while the leading stack is empty, so the default configuration incorrectly collapses the intended 4-point divider; leading-only configurations produce the inverse error. Check `trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews`, matching the renamed pre-change stack.
findings.failureMode: Toolbar states whose leading and trailing action sets differ render the page-action divider with the wrong visibility.
findings.title: Base divider visibility on trailing actions

findings.description: `RolesGuard` interprets this value as the minimum role, so `TEAM_MEMBER` authorizes ordinary accepted members as well as admins. A regular member can therefore mint a reusable team invitation despite the endpoint contract and E2E case requiring 403. Use `@Roles("TEAM_ADMIN")`, as the parallel organization invite endpoint does.
findings.failureMode: An authenticated non-admin member posts to `/v2/teams/:teamId/invite` and receives a valid invite instead of 403, allowing unauthorized expansion of team membership.
findings.title: Require the team-admin role for invite creation

findings.description: This endpoint relies solely on `RolesGuard`, but that guard's team lookup does not filter or inspect `membership.accepted`; `Membership.accepted` defaults to false. Therefore even changing the minimum role to `TEAM_ADMIN` still lets a user holding an unaccepted ADMIN invitation mint further team invites. Require an accepted membership in the authorization lookup before invoking `TeamService`.
findings.failureMode: A user invited as a team admin but who has not accepted the membership authenticates and generates valid join links for other users.
findings.title: Reject pending memberships in the invite guard

findings.description: `result` contains both the redeemable token and an `inviteLink` embedding it. The global `ResponseInterceptor` JSON-stringifies every returned object into `responseBody` and emits it at log level, so every request to this new endpoint copies a seven-day team-join credential into application logs. Redact both fields (or suppress response-body logging for this route) before shipping the endpoint.
findings.failureMode: Anyone with access to application logs can extract an unexpired invite URL/token generated by this endpoint and join the target team without receiving the invite from an admin.
findings.title: Keep invite credentials out of response logs

findings.description: For every newly created invite, this returns `invite-link-for-teamId-<id>` while the database row and `inviteLink` use the random `token`. The advertised token therefore cannot be redeemed, does not appear in the returned URL, and is identical across repeated requests for the team; the new endpoint's own success/new-token assertions fail. Return `newToken.token` (or the local `token`).
findings.failureMode: A successful invite request returns a non-secret identifier as `data.token`; consumers using it receive "Invite not found", and repeated requests report the same token.
findings.title: Return the generated token instead of its identifier

findings.description: The changed condition reverses the established mapping: regular teams now get the organization signup/onboarding URL, while organizations and organization sub-teams get `/teams`. Thus every new invite is sent through the wrong acceptance flow for its context. Keep `/teams` for `!isOrgContext` and use signup/onboarding for organization contexts.
findings.failureMode: Following any generated invite URL opens the wrong acceptance flow: regular team invites go to organization onboarding and organization-context invites go to the regular teams page.
findings.title: Restore the invite routes for each team context

findings.description: API v2's enforced `noRestrictedImports` rule rejects direct imports from `@calcom/features`, and Biome reports this changed line as an error. findings.description: When the reader-mode toolbar button dispatches `showReaderMode`, this reducer now sets `displayView` to `.readerModeLongPressAction`. `BrowserViewController.handleDisplayActions` handles that state by adding the current page to the reading list, whereas `.readerMode` calls `toggleReaderMode()`. Thus a normal tap no longer enters or exits Reader Mode and instead shows reading-list feedback; restore `.readerMode` here.
findings.failureMode: Tap the Reader Mode toolbar button on a reader-capable page; the page is added to the reading list (or reports that it already exists) instead of Reader Mode being toggled.
findings.title: Reader-mode taps are routed to the long-press action

findings.description: A Reader Mode tab's `tab.url` is the internal `http://localhost/.../reader-mode/page?...` URL, while normal toolbar updates deliberately use `tab.url?.displayURL` to expose the original article URL. Because reader URLs also satisfy `isWebPage()`, the new `||` branch retains that raw internal URL when canceling edit mode; the reducer then stores it and `LocationView` displays `absoluteString`. Canceling edit via the menu, tab tray, or cancel button while in Reader Mode therefore replaces the visible article URL with the localhost implementation URL. Restore the reader-mode exclusion in this condition.
findings.failureMode: Enter Reader Mode, edit the address bar, then cancel or tap Menu/Tabs; the address bar displays Firefox's localhost reader-mode URL instead of the article URL.
findings.title: Do not put the internal reader URL back in the address bar

findings.description: `.available` means the tap will enable Reader Mode and `.active` means it will disable it, as `toggleReaderMode()` confirms, but this switch now supplies `false` for available and `true` otherwise. With the existing `ToolbarTelemetry` extra construction, an exit tap on an active non-private page now emits `is_private: true` (before this change it emitted `false`), corrupting reader-mode telemetry. Restore `true` for `.available` and `false` otherwise.
findings.failureMode: Tap the Reader Mode button to exit Reader Mode in a normal, non-private tab; the recorded event is classified as private, and the logical enabled/disabled value supplied by the middleware is opposite the resulting state.
findings.title: Reader-mode telemetry state is inverted

findings.description: This change removes the explicit `private` access modifier from `gleanWrapper`, widening an implementation dependency to the entire module and violating the repository's mandatory rule that properties use explicit, minimal access control. Nothing outside `ToolbarTelemetry` reads this property, and parallel telemetry helpers keep the wrapper private, so retain `private let` rather than exposing it.
findings.failureMode: The changed source fails the repository's access-control compliance requirement and exposes the telemetry sink as module-internal API without a caller that needs it.
findings.title: Keep the telemetry dependency private

findings.description: The new `|| iPad()` exemption applies to every onboarding test, not just the unsupported bottom-toolbar case. `testFirstRunTourDarkMode` explicitly selects Dark on iPad; this branch now skips the existing Light reset, and the app's theme manager stores that choice in persistent `UserDefaults`, so the iPad full-functional job continues with a Dark theme instead of the Light baseline. findings.description: This handles an asynchronous system alert with only a 0.5-second existence wait and then calls `tap()` without checking hittability. If the prompt appears later or its button is still animating on a slower simulator, the alert remains/blocking or the tap fails, and the shared helper times out waiting for the URL text in every copy/share caller. Use the established system-alert pattern that waits for the button to become hittable before tapping.

findings.description: The `<=` executes one extra iteration after all extracted keys have been processed. For a normal keyed command in cluster mode such as `GET foo`, the result contains one key at argv[1], but the extra pass uses the zero-initialized next entry (argv[0], `GET`) and writes `slot_buffer[1]` beyond a one-element allocation; because those strings hash to different slots, the command is rejected as CROSSSLOT. Results at or beyond the six-entry inline-buffer boundary can instead derive an arbitrary argv index and crash. Restore the strict `< keys_result->numkeys` bound.
findings.failureMode: A normal keyed cluster command is rejected as CROSSSLOT and performs an out-of-bounds write; larger key results can dereference an invalid argv entry and crash the server.
findings.title: Stop slot extraction before the result boundary

findings.description: The new `malloc`/`free` calls violate the repository's required allocator-wrapper contract, and `server.h` marks both APIs deprecated. The mandated `make REDIS_CFLAGS="-Werror"` therefore fails while compiling `cluster.c` (the two `free` sites fail as well), so this head cannot pass the required build. Remove this unused temporary buffer, or use `zmalloc`/`zfree` consistently.
findings.failureMode: The repository's required `-Werror` build fails on the newly deprecated libc allocator calls.
findings.title: Replace direct allocation that breaks the required build

findings.description: The new `== '1'` guard makes BUILD002 run precisely for the first servicing patch, while `Baseline.Designer.props` still describes 9.0.0. This transition needs to skip the stale baseline at patch 1 (`!= '1'`) and enforce the check after the 10.0 baseline is established.
findings.failureMode: Building Microsoft.AspNetCore.AzureAppServices.HostingStartup in the new 10.0.1 servicing configuration leaves the 9.0 System.Text.Json baseline item unused, causing ResolveCustomReferences to emit BUILD002 and fail the build.
findings.title: Skip the stale dependency baseline for patch 1

findings.description: The new vector lists seven command tokens (`HSETEX`, key, `KEEPTTL`, `FIELDS`, count, field, value) but declares `argc` as 6. `rewriteClientCommandVector` consumes only six varargs, so the propagated/AOF command omits `newobj` and becomes a wrong-arity `HSETEX ... FIELDS 1 <field>`. Replicas reject every successful `HINCRBYFLOAT`; with the supported `propagation-error-behavior panic-on-replicas` setting this immediately crashes the replica, while the default leaves its value stale. Pass 7 as the vector length.
findings.failureMode: Configure a replica with `propagation-error-behavior panic-on-replicas`, then execute `HINCRBYFLOAT h f 1.1` on its primary; the malformed propagated HSETEX triggers a wrong-arity error and the replica aborts. Under the default ignore behavior, the replica instead keeps the pre-increment value.
findings.title: Rewrite HINCRBYFLOAT with seven arguments

findings.description: When `HINCRBYFLOAT` targets a live field with an expiry, this changed call omits `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL`, so `hashTypeSet` persists the field on the primary. Once the propagation vector is made valid, `HSETEX KEEPTTL` preserves the old expiry on replicas/AOF replay, leaving the primary and its durable/replicated state with different TTLs; even independently, the existing local TTL-preservation test now fails. Keep `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` on this local write; only the propagation rewrite needed to change.
findings.failureMode: Run `HSETEX h EX 100 FIELDS 1 f 1` followed by `HINCRBYFLOAT h f 1.1`; the primary changes the field TTL from 100 to -1, so the field no longer expires even though HINCRBYFLOAT is required to retain that TTL.
findings.title: Preserve the field TTL on the primary update

findings.description: This helper is still called only within `t_hash.c`, but the change removes its `static` storage class. findings.failureMode: The built `t_hash.o` now exposes `addHashFieldToReply` as a global symbol, creating an unintended link-visible API and making a same-named definition in another linked object a duplicate-symbol failure.

findings.description: Workflow inputs and outputs are persisted with the default `json.dumps`, which stores non-ASCII characters as `\uXXXX`; the removed expression converted a Unicode keyword to that serialized form, but the new helper only escapes LIKE metacharacters. findings.description: When the IRIS text index is disabled and the query contains `%`, `_`, or `\`, `escape_like_pattern` prefixes those characters with backslashes, but this SQL declares `|` as the escape character. IRIS therefore treats the inserted backslashes as literal text and the special characters as wildcards, so a search such as `50%` does not match a document containing `50%`. Change the SQL to declare backslash as its ESCAPE character.
findings.failureMode: With IRIS_TEXT_INDEX disabled, searching stored text `50% discount` for `50%` returns no document because the pattern requires a literal backslash before a wildcard.
findings.title: Match IRIS ESCAPE character to helper output

findings.description: ClickZetta connections are configured for quote-based string-literal escaping, but this Python literal emits `ESCAPE '\\'` with two backslash characters in the SQL string. SQL LIKE requires the ESCAPE expression to be one character, so when full-text search falls back to this method the new query is rejected instead of returning fallback results. Emit `ESCAPE '\'` in the generated SQL so the expression is a single backslash.
findings.failureMode: When ClickZetta full-text search throws and calls _search_by_like, cursor.execute rejects the fallback query because its ESCAPE literal contains two characters, leaving retrieval with an error rather than fallback documents.
findings.title: Use a one-character ClickZetta escape literal

The registered type check now emits that requirement plus cascading route errors, and typed ESLint treats every `useWatch` result as unsafe (four new errors); restoring `strict: true` makes those lint errors disappear. findings.description: This field always writes the selected status to `trigger.expect`, even when the posture selector says “Stays in”. A proactive status trigger must start after the selected status and expect the other statuses; the existing canonical mapper reads the selected proactive status from `after`. For example, “Stays in Not Ready for 30s” is currently serialized with no `after` and `expect: [not-ready]`, so it watches for the absence of Not Ready instead of timing from entry into Not Ready. Switch the binding by posture and populate the complementary `expect` statuses for proactive triggers.
findings.failureMode: A user-created proactive work-pool status automation monitors the opposite condition and fires at the wrong time or not at all.
findings.title: Store proactive work-pool status in `after`

findings.description: This status selector remains bound to `trigger.expect` after choosing the proactive “Stays in” posture. The canonical work-queue mapping instead places the chosen status in `after` and all other statuses in `expect`. Thus “Stays in Paused for 30s” is saved with no start event and with Paused as the event whose absence is measured, producing the inverse automation. Bind the selected proactive status to `after` and derive the complementary expected statuses.
findings.failureMode: A user-created proactive work-queue status automation monitors the inverse of the selected status and fires at the wrong time or not at all.
findings.title: Store proactive work-queue status in `after`

findings.description: The new status controls render with an empty value, while the template defaults provide neither `expect` nor `after` and the schema makes both optional. Selecting Deployment status and clicking Next without choosing an option therefore passes validation and emits a reactive trigger whose empty `expect` matches every deployment event. Populate each status template default with its established Not Ready status so the dropdown and payload always start with a concrete status; work-pool and work-queue have the same blank state.
findings.failureMode: Leaving the initially blank status dropdown untouched emits a status-template trigger that fires on any event for the matched resource.
findings.title: Initialize status templates with a status

findings.description: For proactive posture the selector only writes the chosen status to `after`; it never sets `expect` to the opposite status as the established deployment-status mapper does. An empty `expect` matches any event, so if a custom/integration event uses the deployment as its primary resource while the deployment remains Ready/Not Ready, that unrelated event increments the bucket and cancels the “Stays in” trigger. Derive the opposite status into `expect` and keep it synchronized when posture changes.
findings.failureMode: A non-status event on a deployment can resolve its proactive status bucket, preventing the automation from firing even though the deployment remained in the selected status.
findings.title: Set the terminating status for proactive deployments

findings.description: All four newly added proactive forms expose `within` with a minimum of 0, and the wizard's Zod schema also accepts it, but the API contract requires at least 10 seconds. A user can enter 1–9, pass the Trigger step, and then receive an API validation failure when saving (0 is silently normalized to 10). Set the input minimum to 10 and add posture-aware schema validation; the same added `min={0}` occurs in deployment-status line 99 and both work status files line 96.
findings.failureMode: A proactive automation with a 1–9 second window passes client validation but fails to save at the API boundary; a zero value is saved as a different value than entered.
findings.title: Enforce the proactive ten-second minimum

findings.description: `"".split("\n")` is always a one-element array, so after a user types an event and clears the textarea this branch stores `expect: [""]` instead of clearing the field. The backend only gives match-any behavior to an empty `expect` set, and its exact matcher rejects `""` for every normal event name; event processing then skips those events, so the resulting custom automation never fires as the cleared form implies. Filter empty lines and pass `undefined`/`[]` when none remain.
findings.failureMode: Clearing the custom expected-events textarea serializes a blank event string, creating an automation that cannot match normal events instead of an unconstrained event trigger.
findings.title: Do not persist an empty event pattern

findings.description: The Custom, Deployment, and Work Queue handlers place fractional values such as `1.5` into the form, and `EventTriggerSchema` only checks `z.number().min(1)`, while both API trigger models require an integer. Since Next invokes Zod validation from a button rather than native form validation, the fraction passes this step and is rejected when the API model is created. Add integer validation to the wizard schema.
findings.failureMode: A fractional threshold passes the wizard's trigger validation but causes automation creation to fail at the API boundary.
findings.title: Validate thresholds as integers

findings.description: This one threshold field uses `parseInt` while every parallel number input uses `Number`. A number input accepts exponent notation—confirmed `1e2` has `valueAsNumber` 100—but this handler stores `1`; decimal text is likewise silently truncated rather than validated. Convert with `Number` like the sibling fields and let schema validation reject values that are not allowed.
findings.failureMode: A work-pool automation can be saved with a smaller threshold than the user entered, causing it to fire too early.
findings.title: Do not truncate valid numeric threshold input

findings.description: WorkflowRun inputs and outputs are stored as `json.dumps(...)` text, whose default serialization represents non-ASCII characters as `\uXXXX`. Replacing the prior `unicode_escape` conversion with the helper alone builds a pattern containing the literal Unicode keyword, so searching execution logs for a value such as `你好` returns zero rows even when that value is in the inputs or outputs. Keep the JSON Unicode conversion and then escape LIKE metacharacters before adding the wildcards.
findings.failureMode: Keyword searches on non-ASCII workflow inputs/outputs silently omit matching execution logs.
findings.title: Preserve JSON Unicode encoding in workflow search

findings.description: Connections are explicitly configured for ClickZetta's `quote` string-literal mode, where backslashes are not string escapes, but this Python literal emits `ESCAPE '\\'` into SQL (two backslash characters). LIKE requires the ESCAPE expression to be one character, so whenever full-text search falls back to `_search_by_like`, ClickZetta rejects the fallback query instead of returning documents. Emit a single backslash inside the SQL literal (or use a one-character alternative consistently).
findings.failureMode: Any ClickZetta MATCH_ALL failure routes to a fallback query that fails SQL execution.
findings.title: Emit a one-character ClickZetta escape literal

findings.description: The centralized helper prefixes `%`, `_`, and `\` with a backslash, but this query declares `|` as the LIKE escape character. With `IRIS_TEXT_INDEX` disabled, a query such as `50%` therefore becomes `%50\%%`; IRIS treats the backslash literally and `%` as a wildcard, so the document containing `50%` is not returned. Generate `|`-escaped patterns or declare backslash as the SQL escape character.
findings.failureMode: IRIS fallback full-text search returns no or incorrect rows for queries containing LIKE metacharacters.
findings.title: Use the same escape character in IRIS patterns

findings.description: The `not contains` branch now inserts backslash escapes into the pattern but, unlike the parallel LIKE branches, omits `escape="\\"`. On a supported MySQL/OceanBase/SeekDB deployment using `NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES`, a value such as `50%` is tested with `%50\%%` while no escape character is active, so a document whose metadata actually contains `50%` is incorrectly included by NOT LIKE. Pass the same escape argument as the other branches.
findings.failureMode: The not-contains metadata filter returns wrong documents for wildcard characters under a supported MySQL-compatible configuration.
findings.title: Declare the escape character for NOT LIKE

findings.description: The `|| iPad()` condition matches every onboarding test on an iPad, not just the unsupported bottom-placement case. In particular, `testFirstRunTourDarkMode` explicitly switches to Dark, then this condition prevents the existing Light reset. Theme selection is persisted in `UserDefaults.standard`, while the UI-test `ClearProfile` reset only clears profile/documents, so a later test can actually launch in the stale dark theme. findings.description: The paste permission alert is presented asynchronously, but this explicit argument cuts the repository helper's normal 5-second wait down to 0.5 seconds and silently proceeds if it has not appeared. On a loaded simulator the alert can arrive after that deadline, remain blocking, and prevent the URL bar from receiving the paste; `mozWaitForValueContains` then fails. Keep the normal bounded wait (or otherwise synchronize with the alert) before validating the pasted value.
findings.failureMode: A paste permission alert appearing more than 0.5 seconds after the paste action is left undismissed, causing helper callers to time out validating the URL.

findings.description: The new `Task` defers every onboarding action even though this closure and `OnboardingService` are already main-actor isolated. In the compact onboarding view, a forward tap calls `handleBottomButtonAction` and then immediately posts `.screenChanged`; previously `.forward*` completed synchronously and updated `pageCount` before that notification. findings.description: This selector writes the chosen status to `trigger.expect` even for Proactive/“Stays in”. With Proactive + Not Ready, a later Ready event is not one of the expected events and cannot cancel the absence window, so the automation can fire after the pool has already recovered. The established mapping uses the selected status in `after` and all other pool statuses in `expect`; implement that mapping and clear stale posture-specific values.
findings.failureMode: A proactive work-pool automation can fire after the pool has left the selected status because recovery events are not expected/counted.
findings.title: Serialize proactive pool statuses with `after` and recovery events

findings.description: This selector writes the chosen status to `trigger.expect` for both postures. With Proactive + Paused, a subsequent Ready event is not expected and does not cancel the absence window, so the automation can fire although the queue no longer remains paused. The established mapping puts Paused in `after` and every other queue status in `expect`; apply that mapping and clear stale values.
findings.failureMode: A proactive work-queue automation can fire after the queue has left the selected status because recovery events are not expected/counted.
findings.title: Serialize proactive queue statuses with `after` and recovery events

findings.description: For Proactive posture this callback updates only `trigger.after`; it never sets `trigger.expect` to the opposite deployment status. Thus “Stays in Not Ready” is serialized with `after: [not-ready]` and an empty (or stale, if posture was toggled) `expect`. The backend treats an empty expectation as any event, while the established deployment-status mapping expects `ready`, so unrelated deployment events can suppress the timer and stale same-status values can produce an invalid template. Set `after` to the selected status and `expect` to its opposite, clearing stale values when posture changes.
findings.failureMode: A proactive deployment-status automation can be resolved by the wrong deployment event or retain the previously selected same-status expectation, so it does not reliably fire when a deployment remains in the selected status.
findings.title: Populate the recovery event for proactive deployments

findings.description: `"".split("\n")` is `[""]`, so `lines.length > 0` is always true. Clearing the textarea stores `expect: [""]` instead of removing the expectation; an executed component test confirms that exact form value. The backend's exact matcher does not consider any real event equal to the empty string, so this custom trigger never opens a bucket, whereas an omitted/empty `expect` intentionally matches any event. Trim/filter empty lines and pass `undefined` (or `[]`) when none remain.
findings.failureMode: After a user clears the custom expected-events textarea, the saved trigger silently stops matching all real events instead of reverting to the schema's any-event behavior.
findings.title: Drop blank lines before storing custom events

The checked-in baseline still identifies 9.0.0 while `PreviousAspNetCoreReleaseVersion` now evaluates to 10.0.0, so disabling `EnsureBaselineIsUpdated` lets 10.0.1 packages build against a stale 9.0 baseline and can miss a dependency removal relative to 10.0.0. findings.description: The repository instructions require this servicing baseline to be copied from the released `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref` 10.0.0 package, whose normalized `PlatformManifest.txt` records file version `10.0.25.52411`; this new file instead records `10.0.25.52413` for 141 managed assemblies. The SDK uses these values to resolve platform/package conflicts by file version, so it can discard a package assembly at version 52412 or 52413 even though the installed 10.0.0 shared framework only supplies 52411. Copy the released manifest values instead.
findings.failureMode: A framework-dependent application references an assembly build with the same assembly version and file version 10.0.25.52412 or .52413; conflict resolution treats the falsely newer platform entry as the winner, omits the package assembly from publish output, and the app runs against the older 10.0.0 shared-framework implementation.
findings.title: Use the released 10.0.0 platform file versions
